content.intro: In this lesson, you will study string formatting and text blocks with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you process text correctly while accounting for immutability, equality, and Unicode. In this lesson, focus on formatted() and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: String values are immutable, so methods return new results rather than changing existing text. Compare contents with `equals`, and distinguish UTF-16 code units from Unicode code points and visible graphemes. Apply that reasoning specifically to formatted() and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

items.title: String.format()
items.text: String values are immutable sequences of text. Use value equality for text content, understand Unicode code points for international text, and prefer StringBuilder for repeated concatenation in loops.
